judged_text: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters CalDAV calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first array element) only, so per-destination invocations from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents can never select any other host's calendar. Collective multi-host bookings with Apple/CalDAV destinations create the event only on the first host's calendar (or on none when the filter matches nothing for the invoked credential), silently skipping the remaining hosts' calendars.

record.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters CalDAV calendars to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (the first array element) only, so per-destination invocations from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents can never select any other host's calendar. Collective multi-host bookings with Apple/CalDAV destinations create the event only on the first host's calendar (or on none when the filter matches nothing for the invoked credential), silently skipping the remaining hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService.createEvent), the CalDAV calendar selection is hard-coded to the first destination calendar: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then `.filter((c) => mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : true)`. Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination, but BaseCalendarService ignores any per-invocation destination/externalId and will always filter by the first array element. This means multi-destination collective bookings can only create on the first host’s CalDAV/Apple calendar (or none if the first externalId isn’t present for the invoked credential), skipping the rest.
